references.text: The law on restitution for theft: [ref:2 Mos 22:1|Exodus 22:1] states that the thief must repay fourfold. Zacchaeus' promise to repay fourfold (τετραπλοῦν) reflects exactly this provision.
[ref:2 Mos 22:4|Exodus 22:4] describes restitution rules for theft. Zacchaeus exceeds the law's minimum requirement by voluntarily giving fourfold restitution to those he has defrauded.
[ref:4 Mos 5:6-7|Numbers 5:6-7] deals with confession of sin and full restitution plus an additional fifth. Zacchaeus goes far beyond this requirement by promising to repay fourfold.

In [ref:1 Sam 12:3|1 Samuel 12:3], Samuel asks if he has taken anything from anyone unjustly. Zacchaeus openly admits that he has done wrong and offers generous restitution—a contrast to Samuel's innocence.

[ref:Ordsp 21:17|Proverbs 21:17] warns that the one who loves wealth will suffer lack, while Zacchaeus shows generosity by giving half of his possessions to the poor, testifying to a transformed heart.

Isaiah urges sharing bread with the hungry in [ref:Jes 58:7|Isaiah 58:7]. Zacchaeus' decision to give half of his wealth to the poor is a practical fulfillment of the prophet's call to justice and mercy.

[ref:Esek 33:15|Ezekiel 33:15] says that the wicked shall live if they restore what they have stolen and walk in the ways of life. Zacchaeus' actions—making restitution and sharing with the poor—illustrate precisely this repentance that leads to life.
In [ref:Luk 3:8|Luke 3:8], John the Baptist demands fruits worthy of repentance. Zacchaeus' concrete actions—giving to the poor and making restitution for wrongs—are exactly such fruits.
[ref:Luk 3:14|Luke 3:14] warns against extorting money from people by force. Zacchaeus, a tax collector who overcharged, admits that he has extorted (ἐσυκοφάντησα) and now promises to make it right.

In [ref:Luk 11:41|Luke 11:41], Jesus says that what is inside should be given as alms, so that everything becomes clean. Zacchaeus' generosity toward the poor is an expression of inner transformation.

Jesus urges in [ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33] to sell possessions and give alms. Zacchaeus gives half of his possessions to the poor, thereby demonstrating willingness to renounce wealth for the sake of God's kingdom.

[ref:Luk 18:22-23|Luke 18:22-23] tells of the rich man who went away sorrowful when Jesus told him to sell all and give to the poor. Zacchaeus stands in sharp contrast: he voluntarily and gladly gives half of all he owns.

[ref:2 Kor 8:2|2 Corinthians 8:2] describes the churches' abundant generosity amid poverty. Zacchaeus' radical generosity illustrates the same spiritual transformation that makes people willing to give generously.
[ref:1 Tim 6:18|1 Timothy 6:18] urges the rich to do good, be rich in good deeds, and be generous. Zacchaeus is an example of a wealthy man who does exactly this after meeting Jesus.
